refnamediv.refpurpose: Create an Internet or Unix domain server socket

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.parameters;
address
The type of socket created is determined by the transport specified using standard URL formatting: transport://target.
For Internet Domain sockets such as TCP and UDP, the target portion of the address parameter should consist of a hostname or IP address followed by a colon and a port number. For Unix domain sockets, the target portion should point to the socket file on the filesystem.
The file of a unix:// or udg:// server is never removed by PHP: it survives fclose and the end of the request, and binding to the same path again fails until the file is deleted. A path longer than the system limit (107 bytes on Linux) is truncated, with an E_NOTICE.
Depending on the environment, Unix domain sockets may not be available. A list of available transports can be retrieved using stream_get_transports. See for a list of built-in transports.
error_code
If the optional error_code and error_message arguments are present they are set when the function fails. error_code is always 0: the system error number of a failed bind() or listen() is not reported, and error_message is the only diagnostic. It is set for a failed TCP bind() (for example Address already in use), but can be empty, for example for a failed listen() or for a Unix domain socket. Note that the error_code and error_message arguments will always be passed by reference.
error_message
See error_code description.
flags
A bitmask field which may be set to any combination of STREAM_SERVER_BIND and STREAM_SERVER_LISTEN. With 0 or STREAM_SERVER_LISTEN alone, the socket is neither bound nor listening, and with STREAM_SERVER_BIND alone, a TCP socket is bound but does not listen, so connections are refused.
For UDP (udp://) and datagram Unix domain (udg://) sockets, you must use STREAM_SERVER_BIND alone as the flags parameter: with the default value, stream_socket_server returns &false;.
context
A stream context, or &null; to use the default context. The socket context options backlog and so_reuseport are used by the server, see Socket context options. SO_REUSEADDR is always set: a second UDP server can bind the same port, while a second TCP server cannot, unless so_reuseport is enabled.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns the created stream, or &false; on error.
